steps.text: The cold spell of springtide.
It hearkens me back to many scenes of the past: my academic pursuits, my career in business, my training in the martial arts, and my entrance into politics.
In those bygone times, we were inseparable. Kind friends and mentors were always there for us, each of them hoping to realize their own grand aspirations.
What about now?
The green bricks have yet to be cleaned. Spring has long since begun, yet the snow lingers, white as pearls.
It is impossible to know what the man behind the door thinks when it is shut. All you are certain of is that, when it opens, what you know is merely what he wants you to know.
He lifts his head. The door lets out a creak.

steps.name: Boatman
steps.text: Mr. Liang.

steps.name: Lee
steps.text: Liang Xun... Long time no see.

steps.name: Liang Xun
steps.text: Indeed. It's been a while.

steps.name: Liang Xun
steps.text: You've ventured far, Lee.

steps.name: Lee
steps.text: It was a long journey, and I'd be lying if I said it wasn't arduous. How gaudy of you then, Mr. Liang, to have me travel all this way just to deliver this small trinket.

steps.name: Liang Xun
steps.text: All will be explained as soon as I have the time.

steps.name: Liang Xun
steps.text: I must thank you too, Master Shen. It's early spring. There must be many a traveler seeking to make their way across the waters.

steps.name: Boatman
steps.text: Not at all. I accepted the job, so naturally it's my top priority.

steps.name: Boatman
steps.text: But now that I've brought him... I think I'll head back to the docks.

steps.name: Boatman
steps.text: Oh right. We ran into a bit of trouble in the city. Lee can fill you in on the details.

steps.name: Liang Xun
steps.text: Trouble...?

steps.name: Boatman
steps.text: You'd best be careful too, sir.

steps.name: Boatman
steps.text: I'll take my leave. The docks must be low on manpower by now. I should hurry back.

steps.name: Liang Xun
steps.text: Right. Thank you for your work.

steps.name: Lee
steps.text: 'Make your way to Shangshu via Zhengshan, and find a boatman named Shen.'

steps.name: Lee
steps.text: See how far your reputation gets you, Mr. Liang? You sent for me with just that one sentence.

steps.name: Liang Xun
steps.text: This isn't exactly your first time visiting Shangshu.

steps.name: Lee
steps.text: So what kind of man is this Master Shen?

steps.name: Liang Xun
steps.text: Just a trustworthy boatman. And experienced boatmen can be trusted with your life.

steps.name: Lee
steps.text: Fair enough.

steps.name: Liang Xun
steps.text: Come to think of it, I haven't been introduced to these two...

steps.name: Mr. Nothing
steps.text: (Good gracious, how did I not notice? So this 'Mr. Liang' is the magistrate of Shangshu?!)

steps.name: Kroos
steps.text: (I'm getting pretty used to you overreacting to stuff you missed. What's that mean for us, though?)

steps.name: Mr. Nothing
steps.text: (He's the head of the city!)

steps.name: Kroos
steps.text: (Knowing how Yan ranks officials, though, doesn't that make him a whole lot lower than Wei Yenwu?)

steps.name: Lee
steps.text: These two are my... business partners.

steps.name: Mr. Nothing
steps.text: It is an honor, Mr. Liang. I'm Ch'u...

steps.name: Mr. Nothing
steps.text: Wu-yu. Please call me Mr. Nothing.

steps.name: Kroos
steps.text: And I'm Kroos. I'm an Operator on deployment from Rhodes Island Pharmaceuticals, which has an ongoing business relationship with Mr. Lee.

steps.name: Kroos
steps.text: We only bumped into each other in Shangshu by chance, though. Anyway, it's a pleasure to meet you, Mr. Liang.

steps.name: Liang Xun
steps.text: By chance? And here I thought you hired Messengers to escort you from Lungmen...

steps.name: Lee
steps.text: So you ARE aware that Messengers exist? Then perhaps you should've hired them to run your errands instead of me.

steps.name: Liang Xun
steps.text: It was no trivial matter, and the journey was long. I couldn't trust just anyone.

steps.name: Lee
steps.text: But you could trust me? Give me a break. What was I supposed to do if I ran into bandits on the way?

steps.name: Liang Xun
steps.text: If you thought it a hassle, you could have written back and refused.

steps.name: Lee
steps.text: Please, like there'd be another chance with that trinket of yours. By the time your letter made it to me, the smugglers were already in Lungmen.

steps.name: Lee
steps.text: When did I have time to write back and tell you to find somebody else? I had to get someone looking into them straight away, smashing up their hideout too, while we were at it.

steps.name: Lee
steps.text: *Sigh* Fortunately, the kids working for me are more than capable of holding the fort. Otherwise I wouldn't have time for this errand of yours.

steps.name: Kroos
steps.text: (Sounds like Waai Fu's MO to me... and I'm guessing Mr. Lee took this as an excuse to skip town rather than deal with everything on his plate.)

steps.name: Liang Xun
steps.text: Seeing as you are Lee's business partners, we shouldn't be discussing this at the door. Please, come in. We have enough guest rooms for everyone.

steps.name: Lee
steps.text: What an honor to be personally received by Shangshu's magistrate. Best we accept, then.

steps.name: Liang Xun
steps.text: Please, this way.

steps.name: Mr. Nothing
steps.text: You have our thanks, Mr. Liang.

steps.name: Mr. Nothing
steps.text: Benefactor, we were just worrying about where to stay the night, and there's still some time until our meeting. Why not get some rest here?

steps.name: Kroos
steps.text: Hmm...

steps.name: Mr. Nothing
steps.text: Benefactor?

steps.name: Kroos
steps.text: Nothing... Guess I'm just tired.

steps.name: Kroos
steps.text: Mr. Lee, do we have to tell Mr. Liang about what just happened?

steps.name: Lee
steps.text: Yes, we should...

steps.name: Lee
steps.text: Look at the sky. It's filled with clouds. It'll probably rain tonight—

steps.name: Liang Xun
steps.text: ...? What's the matter, Lee?

steps.name: Lee
steps.text: Nothing...

steps.name: Lee
steps.text: Some landscapes flashed through my mind, is all... Maybe it's been way too long since I last visited Shangshu, and the nostalgia is getting to me.

steps.name: Street Youth
steps.text: Miss Du... How did it go?

steps.name: Miss Du
steps.text: How did what go? That ugly old Zheng gave me an earful.

steps.name: Street Youth
steps.text: What should we do, then?

steps.name: Miss Du
steps.text: I told you. We can't always listen to them.

steps.name: Miss Du
steps.text: If that's all we ever do, we won't have a future.

steps.name: Miss Du
steps.text: Just do as I say.

steps.name: Street Youth
steps.text: Alright. I'll call everyone up.

steps.name: Miss Du
steps.text: Mm-hm.

steps.name: Street Youth
steps.text: How will you deal with the Lungmenite now?

steps.name: Miss Du
steps.text: I'll go see him myself.

steps.name: Miss Du
steps.text: Some things are best discussed with an open heart.

steps.name: Lee
steps.text: How about a drink?

steps.name: Liang Xun
steps.text: I'll pass. I have work later.

steps.name: Lee
steps.text: You had me travel thousands of li to bring you a wine cup, and you won't indulge me with one little drink?

steps.name: Lee
steps.text: I went through hell and high water for this thing, you know.

steps.name: Liang Xun
steps.text: Drink makes fools of us all.

steps.name: Lee
steps.text: Ah, 'drink makes fools of us all...'

steps.name: Lee
steps.text: One of the Liang Xun of yesteryear's favorite sayings. Full glad I am to know that Mr. Liang still cannot hold his liquor.

steps.name: Liang Xun
steps.text: And full glad I am to know that you're still that good old foulmouthed Lee.

steps.name: Liang Xun
steps.text: I've sent someone to investigate what happened at Xingyu Inn.

steps.name: Lee
steps.text: I doubt things are as simple as they seem. If you really don't know, then no need to stir up the hornet's nest. Such is the society we live in.

steps.name: Lee
steps.text: Especially when simply waiting for me to leave the city would more or less solve all our troubles.

steps.name: Lee
steps.text: Are you sure you don't need to check on the cup? The roads were bumpy. I could very well have flattened it under my posterior.

steps.name: Liang Xun
steps.text: If you didn't feel it worth mentioning, then it must be safe and sound.

steps.name: Lee
steps.text: Haha...

steps.name: Lee
steps.text: I say you take a look anyway. I hand-delivered this beauty all the way from Lungmen, after all.

steps.name: Liang Xun
steps.text: So this is it...

steps.name: Lee
steps.text: Now, indulge my curiosity: what makes it so special? At the price it was going for in the smugglers' auctions, it may as well have been a buy-one-get-one-free sale.

steps.name: Lee
steps.text: A rumor circulating among the smugglers did catch my attention though. Apparently, this thing was at the center of a ghost story in the village it was found.

steps.name: Liang Xun
steps.text: Do tell.

steps.name: Lee
steps.text: They say the cup can make the things around it... come to life.

steps.name: Liang Xun
steps.text: Is there any proof?

steps.name: Lee
steps.text: If there were any proof to a ghost story, you'd have heard about it on the news by now. I only know the rumors.

steps.name: Liang Xun
steps.text: And what of the smugglers?

steps.name: Lee
steps.text: All taken to the L.G.D.

steps.name: Liang Xun
steps.text: That's good to hear.

steps.name: Liang Xun
steps.text: Actually, there is another matter I would like you to take care of.

steps.name: Lee
steps.text: Well, you summoned me all the way from Lungmen. You may as well get your money's worth while I'm here.

steps.name: Lee
steps.text: But for now...

steps.name: Liang Xun
steps.text: Hoh... It seems you won't let me go without sharing a drink with you.

steps.name: Liang Xun
steps.text: We'll save business for later, then. You haven't changed, old friend. Carefree as always.

steps.name: Lee
steps.text: Come, sit.

steps.name: Liang Xun
steps.text: Now you're the master?

steps.name: Liang Xun
steps.text: How are your days in Lungmen? I heard you're a private investigator now?

steps.name: Lee
steps.text: Right... And Huai's daughter is staying with me, too. You know, Huai, the kung fu lunatic.

steps.name: Liang Xun
steps.text: Ah, no wonder you asked me to look into his whereabouts all of a sudden.

steps.name: Lee
steps.text: I've been taking care of Waai Fu for a while now, actually. I even went to her university graduation ceremony in his place. Am I supposed to walk her down the aisle when she gets married too?

steps.name: Lee
steps.text: Waai Fu's a good girl, but she's got a terrible father.

steps.name: Liang Xun
steps.text: His daughter... She's grown so much.

steps.name: Lee
steps.text: Time flies, Liang Xun.

steps.name: Liang Xun
steps.text: Indeed...

steps.name: Lee
steps.text: I heard you took up a job in government, and with your personality and skills I figured you had a bright future ahead of you. Never did I imagine that our reunion would take so many years though.

steps.name: Liang Xun
steps.text: I'm sure everyone will be happy to hear you managed to get back on your feet.

steps.name: Lee
steps.text: Hardly. I just realized that some things aren't nearly as much of a headache as figuring out how to put food on the table.

steps.name: Liang Xun
steps.text: It's been a while since I had your cooking...

steps.name: Lee
steps.text: You're a big shot who governs a large city. Stop looking back so fondly on the tough times we struggled through.

steps.name: Lee
steps.text: Instead, think back to the times when we lacked opportunities to use our talents, and make sure the youngsters in your city have them. Isn't that what used to vex you the most?

steps.name: Liang Xun
steps.text: Indeed...

steps.name: Lee
steps.text: Hmm, still, glad to see you're still the type to never, ever, hold a woman.

steps.name: Lee
steps.text: I was worried I'd come to Shangshu only to find you'd started a family. Which would make me—

steps.name: Gentle Female Voice
steps.text: Mr. Liang... You have a guest?

steps.name: Liang Xun
steps.text: *Cough*...

steps.name: Liang Xun
steps.text: Miss Ning... I'm afraid now is not a good time...

steps.name: Lee
steps.text: —What do you mean, now isn't a good time? I'm just a Messenger. I'll be taking my leave soon!

steps.name: Miss Ning
steps.text: Good evening, Mr. Liang... and... Mr. Messenger?

steps.name: Lee
steps.text: That's right, young miss.

steps.name: Lee
steps.text: (Explain.)

steps.name: Liang Xun
steps.text: (She's a coworker.)

steps.name: Lee
steps.text: (Mighty fine coworker you have over at this hour.)

steps.name: Liang Xun
steps.text: (It's barely past dinnertime.)

steps.name: Miss Ning
steps.text: Oh.

steps.name: Miss Ning
steps.text: Might you have forgotten our engagement tonight?

steps.name: Liang Xun
steps.text: No, it's just...

steps.name: Lee
steps.text: Please, don't mind me. I have a few errands that just came to mind.

steps.name: Lee
steps.text: I'll leave you to it, Mr. Liang. If you need anything else... Ugh, try to finish your business first.

steps.name: Liang Xun
steps.text: Wait, Lee—

steps.name: Lee
steps.text: Well, seems I'm in trouble.

steps.name: Kroos
steps.text: Nothing, mate... We're just looking for some grub. Does this really need to be such a big deal?

steps.name: Kroos
steps.text: It's not like Nian's here. I'm fine with whatever. No one's going to complain.

steps.name: Mr. Nothing
steps.text: Absolutely not, my benefactor! I must apologize for what happened earlier by finding you the very finest establishment!

steps.name: Kroos
steps.text: Okay... so how come we're in some empty alley?

steps.name: Mr. Nothing
steps.text: You don't understand. Everyone in Yan has a handful of hole-in-the-wall eateries they hold dear to their hearts. Flavors that simply cannot be enjoyed anywhere else, no matter how reputable.

steps.name: Mr. Nothing
steps.text: You savor the memories, and taste the feelings, and, uh...

steps.name: Kroos
steps.text: You're not even a local... How can anywhere here be dear to your heart?

steps.name: Kroos
steps.text: Now put that travel guide away.

steps.name: Mr. Nothing
steps.text: If you insist.

steps.name: Kroos
steps.text: Do you have some kind of four-dimensional pocket? Where are you keeping all those weird books...?

steps.name: Kroos
steps.text: And you keep taking us down alleyways too... Trying to lure out the people who attacked us earlier?

steps.name: Mr. Nothing
steps.text: We're wards of the city's magistrate! What do we have to be afraid of?

steps.name: Mr. Nothing
steps.text: Besides, they are hardly the upstanding sort! Rather than wait for them to come to us, I say we nip this in the bud before our rendezvous with the others.

steps.name: Kroos
steps.text: The safest play would be to hole up in the Liang estate and contact the closest field office to send Operators to meet us in Shangshu... Hmm...

steps.name: Mr. Nothing
steps.text: I've been meaning to ask, but are there many Yanese at Rhodes Island?

steps.name: Kroos
steps.text: Now that you mention it, I don't think there's all that many, but it also feels like I run into them just about everywhere. It's strange—

a.text: Infected walking freely in the city?

steps.name: Mr. Nothing
steps.text: Benefactor, watch out—

steps.name: Kroos
steps.text: Urgh—

steps.name: Imposing Man
steps.text: Such a lightning-fast reaction.

steps.name: Imposing Man
steps.text: What a surprise.

steps.name: Mr. Nothing
steps.text: What is this about—
Mr. Nothing thinks fast and moves even faster, as do most kung fu practitioners.
However, the brawny man strikes more quickly than even the skip of Mr. Nothing's heartbeat, reaching his throat.

steps.name: Imposing Man
steps.text: Don't try anything funny.

steps.name: Kroos
steps.text: Nothing! Don't do it, mate!

steps.name: Imposing Man
steps.text: Do you know your companion's identity? Did you know she belongs to an Infected organization?

steps.name: Mr. Nothing
steps.text: Haha... Benefactor, to be quite honest, I'm afraid I couldn't do anything even if I wanted to...

steps.name: Mr. Nothing
steps.text: What's more... This is a government official.

steps.name: Imposing Man
steps.text: What a strange fan you wield. You are a master of your techniques, but you have yet to kill.

steps.name: Imposing Man
steps.text: At least you are aware of your weaknesses.

steps.name: Kroos
steps.text: Have we met...?

steps.name: Imposing Man
steps.text: We have not.

steps.name: Imposing Man
steps.text: However, it seems you two are somehow connected to the deputy minister of the Central Judicial Office.

steps.name: Kroos
steps.text: You mean... Leizi?

steps.name: Kroos
steps.text: Right! I saw you in our Operational Records before! You're...!

steps.name: Taihe
steps.text: Taihe, Deputy Monitor Censor of the Department of Discipline and Supervision.

steps.name: Mr. Nothing
steps.text: De-department of Discipline and Supervision...?!

steps.name: Taihe
steps.text: Infected, what is your purpose here in Shangshu?

steps.name: Taihe
steps.text: What happened at Kou-wu City? Why did Dusk leave the mountains?

steps.name: Taihe
steps.text: And how is Rhodes Island involved?

steps.name: Mr. Nothing
steps.text: (Benefactor, is this... about Miss Dusk?)

steps.name: Taihe
steps.text: Keeping quiet, are we?

steps.name: Kroos
steps.text: There is no need to probe Rhodes Island, sir. We've already gone through all the formalities... as Infected.

steps.name: Kroos
steps.text: If you want to know about our Operators' private lives, though, there is truly nothing I can tell you.

steps.name: Kroos
steps.text: Not that I know anything anyway.

steps.name: Taihe
steps.text: Operators...?

steps.name: Taihe
steps.text: A bestial Sui taking an office job? Unheard of.

steps.name: Taihe
steps.text: It seems the Central Judicial Office was highly negligent in its handling of Rhodes Island.

steps.name: Kroos
steps.text: So you tailed us, huh...?

steps.name: Taihe
steps.text: Not at all.

steps.name: Kroos
steps.text: But you won't let us go?

steps.name: Taihe
steps.text: That depends on how cooperative you are.

steps.name: Young Male Voice
steps.text: No need to be so confrontational, Uncle Taihe.

steps.name: Taihe
steps.text: Lord Zuo.

steps.name: Amiable Young Man
steps.text: I've spoken with the other Candleholders to better understand the situation. These... Rhodes Island-related individuals are currently guests of the Shangshu magistrate.

steps.name: Amiable Young Man
steps.text: They may be involved with the Mount Hui-ch'i incident, but they clearly mean no offense. We needn't come to blows.

steps.name: Amiable Young Man
steps.text: My apologies. Uncle Taihe is usually a quiet man, but for whatever reason he is unusually agitated today.

steps.name: Zuo Le
steps.text: I am Zuo Le, a... court Messenger. We will leave it at that.

steps.name: Kroos
steps.text: I'm Kroos, a Rhodes Island Operator.

steps.name: Mr. Nothing
steps.text: Chu Wuyou, otherwise known as Rhodes Island Operator Nothing. Although not yet officially.

steps.name: Zuo Le
steps.text: Ms. Kroos, Mr. Nothing. Please accept my apologies.

steps.name: Zuo Le
steps.text: I understand the transgression was Uncle Taihe's, but allow me to remind you:

steps.name: Zuo Le
steps.text: If you are not too involved with those sisters, I suggest you put an end to that relationship while you still can.

steps.name: Kroos
steps.text: Nian's my friend and coworker, and Dusk's my friend's pain-in-the-rear sister. So is that in the 'while we still can' stage or not?

steps.name: Zuo Le
steps.text: To tell the truth... You've likely already crossed the line.

steps.name: Kroos
steps.text: Thanks for the tip, then.

steps.name: Zuo Le
steps.text: Heh.

steps.name: Zuo Le
steps.text: Ms. Kroos, you're a woman of extraordinary courage and skill.

steps.name: Zuo Le
steps.text: Now we have other business to attend to. Please excuse us.

steps.name: Taihe
steps.text: I hope Magistrate Liang will give the Department of Discipline and Supervision an acceptable answer regarding the Rhodes Island affair.

steps.name: Taihe
steps.text: Excuse us.

steps.name: Mr. Nothing
steps.text: Benefactor! Are you okay?

steps.name: Kroos
steps.text: Haha... That gave me such a start, I sprained my ankle. I'm okay, though.

steps.name: Kroos
steps.text: Nothing, mate.

steps.name: Mr. Nothing
steps.text: Hmm...

steps.name: Mr. Nothing
steps.text: A Messenger accompanied by the Department of Discipline and Supervision's Deputy Monitir Censor as his retainer... What a load of poppycock. They really took us for fools.

steps.name: Mr. Nothing
steps.text: It seems they're also well aware of the bizarre events in which we found ourselves at Kou-wu City and Mount Hui-ch'i.

steps.name: Mr. Nothing
steps.text: Even a fool can glean that the sisters are no ordinary beings, but all this is a little... uh... beyond imagination.

steps.name: Kroos
steps.text: Let's head back to the Liang estate first.

steps.name: Kroos
steps.text: Now's not the time to be wandering around. We need to meet up with them as soon as possible...

steps.name: Kroos
steps.text: Huh...?

steps.name: Mr. Nothing
steps.text: What about him?

steps.name: Kroos
steps.text: Nah... It was probably just some small critter.

steps.name: Liang Xun
steps.text: *Sigh*.

steps.name: Miss Ning
steps.text: 'Tis not like you to sigh so much.

steps.name: Miss Ning
steps.text: Are you so unhappy to see me tonight, my lord?

steps.name: Liang Xun
steps.text: No.

steps.name: Liang Xun
steps.text: Is something the matter?

steps.name: Miss Ning
steps.text: Must I have urgent matters to seek your companionship?

steps.name: Liang Xun
steps.text: No...

steps.name: Miss Ning
steps.text: When shall we take to the mountains and see the plays?

steps.name: Liang Xun
steps.text: The weather is still cold. I heard you've been ill as of late. You should be avoiding the mountains.

steps.name: Miss Ning
steps.text: 'Tis always the case in early spring. It makes me long for the hot tea served at Shuzhou Peak.

steps.name: Liang Xun
steps.text: Right. I will go with you when I have the time.

steps.name: Miss Ning
steps.text: That was your guest, was he not? You were never one to engage in small talk with Messengers.

steps.name: Miss Ning
steps.text: Perhaps you might settle for 'leave the goods there. Stop wasting my time.'?

steps.name: Miss Ning
steps.text: No, I doubt you would say that last part. After all, you are a man of proper etiquette, my lord.

steps.name: Liang Xun
steps.text: Nothing escapes you, Miss Ning.

steps.name: Miss Ning
steps.text: Where is he from?

steps.name: Liang Xun
steps.text: Lungmen.

steps.name: Miss Ning
steps.text: So far away! Ah... He came all this way to see you. I should not have intruded.

steps.name: Liang Xun
steps.text: Not at all. He's not one to mind such trivialities.

steps.name: Miss Ning
steps.text: My, how strange... To think you'd say that about someone.

steps.name: Miss Ning
steps.text: Here I thought you would be the same aloof man to everyone.

steps.name: Liang Xun
steps.text: *Cough*... I don't...

steps.name: Miss Ning
steps.text: What is he doing here?

steps.name: Liang Xun
steps.text: I... I entrusted some matters to him.

steps.name: Miss Ning
steps.text: What sorts of matters?

steps.name: Liang Xun
steps.text: All trivial.

steps.name: Miss Ning
steps.text: So you invited an old friend from a thousand li away only for trivial matters...

steps.name: Miss Ning
steps.text: If you will not tell me, I shan't ask.

steps.name: Miss Ning
steps.text: However, this world is full of hardships. Such is life. If you were to anguish over each and every one of them...

steps.name: Miss Ning
steps.text: You would only be overburdening yourself.

steps.name: Lee
steps.text: Hm?

steps.name: Lee
steps.text: Didn't Liang say this guest room was for me to use as I please?

steps.name: Lee
steps.text: Let's ignore the fact that you came into my room uninvited. Why are you making tea? MY tea, mind you.

steps.name: Miss Du
steps.text: It's not yours, it's Mr. Liang's.

steps.name: Miss Du
steps.text: And I made you a cup too. Satisfied?

steps.name: Lee
steps.text: So you plan to continue your accusations, Miss Du?

steps.name: Miss Du
steps.text: Take a guess.

steps.name: Lee
steps.text: I don't suppose you're bold enough to try anything in such a pretty mansion.

steps.name: Lee
steps.text: Why don't you start by telling me why you're here?

steps.name: Miss Du
steps.text: Heh, aren't you the confident one? Still carefree enough to make conversation with me.

steps.name: Lee
steps.text: Well, you made tea.

steps.name: Miss Du
steps.text: Alright, fine.

steps.name: Miss Du
steps.text: I'll get to the point. I'm here because I need your help.

steps.name: Lee
steps.text: Alright.

steps.name: Miss Du
steps.text: Huh?

steps.name: Miss Du
steps.text: Now that's odd. I thought you'd be more cautious. Why so agreeable?

steps.name: Lee
steps.text: Liang Xun let you into his home. What is there to worry about?

steps.name: Lee
steps.text: Do you know him?

steps.name: Miss Du
steps.text: I pleaded him to let me in, that's all... My father's always had a good relationship with the government.

steps.name: Lee
steps.text: I see.

steps.name: Miss Du
steps.text: Last time we met, I was going to steal your cup.

steps.name: Lee
steps.text: Not mine. Mr. Liang's.

steps.name: Lee
steps.text: Let him deal with the troublesome stuff. I only bother with whatever troubles come my way.

steps.name: Miss Du
steps.text: So you'll believe me...?

steps.name: Lee
steps.text: What reason do I have to hold a grudge against a young lady?

steps.name: Lee
steps.text: *Sigh*... All of us were young once, and all of us have had to put up an act just to save face.

steps.name: Miss Du
steps.text: —W-Who's saving face?! I was—

steps.name: Lee
steps.text: Did you get in a fight with the innkeeper?

steps.name: Miss Du
steps.text: Heh.

steps.name: Miss Du
steps.text: I'm starting to understand just what a terrifying person you are.

steps.name: Miss Du
steps.text: You seem lax and carefree, but you actually know everything like the back of your hand—People like you are the most terrifying.

steps.name: Lee
steps.text: At the very least, I wouldn't attack someone with a chair on our first meeting.

steps.name: Lee
steps.text: Now, tell me what this is about. And be honest, this is a negotiation.

steps.name: Miss Du
steps.text: Innkeeper Zheng... My father took on a job from a court noble. They want that wine cup of yours.

steps.name: Lee
steps.text: About what I figured, but earlier you were helping him with that. Why the sudden change of heart?

steps.name: Miss Du
steps.text: I won't go into the details. It's just... I don't want him to succeed.

steps.name: Lee
steps.text: So?

steps.name: Miss Du
steps.text: Will you not believe me if I don't tell you why?

steps.name: Lee
steps.text: Try not to ask questions that you already know the answer to. You want to come across as sincere.

steps.name: Miss Du
steps.text: If he succeeds, it doesn't matter how big a role I played. He'll make me take full credit for it.

steps.name: Miss Du
steps.text: The Escort Association has made itself a lot of enemies, and, for all the weight it has to throw around, it's stuck by the old rules even now that the Messenger industry has taken off. They're always left out for being slower to react than everyone else.

steps.name: Miss Du
steps.text: That's why my father always told me to keep my mouth shut, to hide my shortcomings.

steps.name: Miss Du
steps.text: He wants me to act like a frivolous playgirl who pisses away his riches. All so no one will give me a second thought.

steps.name: Miss Du
steps.text: Then, I'd secretly run errands for the court, both to curry favor and win over my lackeys.

steps.name: Miss Du
steps.text: Only then will he finally entrust me with the family business.

steps.name: Lee
steps.text: Well, that's an innkeeper for you. Always so calculating.

steps.name: Miss Du
steps.text: But I'm not part of the equation.

steps.name: Miss Du
steps.text: Whether it's the Du Yaoye who will inherit the Association, or the Miss Du who's always throwing money around, both are what others expect me to be.

steps.name: Lee
steps.text: So you want to take this chance to ensure your old man has to stay put and right the ship. That way you won't need to take over as the new innkeeper. Am I getting this right?

steps.name: Miss Du
steps.text: Not quite.

steps.name: Miss Du
steps.text: The royal court doesn't often come to the Association with a job. If this deal falls through, there is no way my father is going to hand me the keys to the Association just yet.

steps.name: Miss Du
steps.text: Most people my age look to me for a way out. I told them that if my father's deal falls through, the Association won't expect anything from us youngsters anymore.

steps.name: Lee
steps.text: But either way you're still waiting for your old man to pass the baton to you. What's the difference?

steps.name: Miss Du
steps.text: That's nothing more than an arrangement to keep us in line. Once I inherit the Association, I will have to follow the rules.

steps.name: Miss Du
steps.text: And the 'rules' go way beyond my father.

steps.name: Lee
steps.text: That's why you've come to me to... uh, help you put on this play of yours?

steps.name: Miss Du
steps.text: That it is.

steps.name: Lee
steps.text: Du Yaoye... Is that your name, my lady?

steps.name: Miss Du
steps.text: W-What about it?

steps.name: Lee
steps.text: 'On this silent autumn night, lingering sorrows yet grapple my heart. A long night that never ceases.' Yaoye refers to the long night from that lovely poem.

steps.name: Miss Du
steps.text: Too bad, I prefer going out at twilight.

steps.name: Lee
steps.text: Since this is a deal though... what's in it for me?

steps.name: Miss Du
steps.text: There's somebody out there, from the royal court, who wants what you have. But you didn't let them have it. Do you understand what that means?

steps.name: Lee
steps.text: My friend never told me to hand it over. Besides, isn't he a member of said court?

steps.name: Miss Du
steps.text: Mr. Liang had you come all this way. He has something else for you, doesn't he?

steps.name: Lee
steps.text: Only trivial matters.

steps.name: Miss Du
steps.text: Whatever. I don't really care. It's just, now that it's come to this you won't be able to pretend you've got nothing to do with it anymore. No matter what you intend.

steps.name: Miss Du
steps.text: I can help you. At the very least, I can guarantee you'll make it back to Lungmen in one piece.

steps.name: Lee
steps.text: Fair point...

steps.name: Lee
steps.text: It's a deal, then.

steps.name: Miss Du
steps.text: It's a deal...

steps.name: Miss Du
steps.text: Heh, talking to you is easier than I expected.

steps.name: Miss Du
steps.text: Relax, I may not want to be the innkeeper, but all my friends my age have more than a few things to say about our elders. And all of them follow my orders.

steps.name: Lee
steps.text: You say you don't want to take over the Association, but aren't you doing the same thing...?

steps.name: Miss Du
steps.text: Times have changed.

steps.name: Lee
steps.text: Right, right.

steps.name: Miss Du
steps.text: I can't help but feel you're hiding something, but fine. It'll be nothing but trouble if they find me here.

steps.name: Miss Du
steps.text: Uhh...

steps.name: Lee
steps.text: Call me Lee.

steps.name: Miss Du
steps.text: —Alright, Lee. We'll meet again!

steps.name: Lee
steps.text: The innkeeper may seem a kind, amiable man, but his daughter...

steps.name: Waai Fu
steps.text: Uncle Lee...

steps.name: Lee
steps.text: Hm?

steps.name: Waai Fu
steps.text: You're visiting Uncle Liang, right?

steps.name: Lee
steps.text: Right... *Sigh*... I really don't want to go on this trip...

steps.name: Lee
steps.text: I'll keep an eye out for your dad.

steps.name: Lee
steps.text: With any luck, I might even drag him back here.

steps.name: Waai Fu
steps.text: Hmm...

steps.name: Waai Fu
steps.text: Thanks.

steps.name: Lee
steps.text: Oh, don't be like that... Don't expect too much either.

steps.name: Lee
steps.text: Yan is a big place, too big to find someone that easily.

steps.name: Lee
steps.text: Waai Fu...

steps.name: Lee
steps.text: Look, I need you to know. It doesn't matter if you're going to tell him off, hammer him with questions, or let bygones be bygones and fawn over him. If I do find him, you'll need to face him on your own.

steps.name: Lee
steps.text: It's only when you catch your fool of a dad's shadow that he'll turn back to look at you. That's the kind of man he is.

steps.name: Lee
steps.text: I'll be in Shangshu for a while. If I hear anything about him, I'll let you know.

steps.name: Lee
steps.text: And... once you're ready, come find me.

steps.name: Waai Fu
steps.text: I understand.

steps.name: Lee
steps.text: *Sigh*.

steps.name: Lee
steps.text: That prick Liang Xun... neglecting his guest like this without so much as telling me his next move...

steps.name: Lee
steps.text: Hm... the tea isn't the best I've had, but the pot is quite the work of art. A fine teapot, indeed...

steps.name: Lee
steps.text: Hmm... A full calligraphy set too... Fairly old-fashioned for a guest room. I see Liang Xun's tastes haven't changed.

steps.name: Lee
steps.text: (Yawn)

steps.name: Lee
steps.text: Phew... That journey took it all out of me.

steps.name: Lee
steps.text: I'm past due for a break. After all that abuse I've taken from him, I'm pooped—

steps.name: Lee
steps.text: —Where am I?

steps.name: Strange Object
steps.text: Ao...
